tasks.short: Research industrial and pollution effects on climate, air quality and weather

steps.what: Research the impact of industrial projects or pollution on climate, air quality or weather

tasks.design: Retain research design, evidence assessment and causal interpretation with the scientist using {DATA_PLATFORM} and {DOCS}. Existing computational tools support the investigation without establishing a new saving in scientific judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Industrial and pollution effects must be distinguished from background variability and confounding influences.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing observations and analytical tools support research.
tasks.still_hard: Establish credible attribution and communicate evidential limits.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible comparisons and challenge apparent causal effects.
tasks.altitude: Own the scientific basis of environmental impact findings.

evidence.claim: Scientific impact research retains interpretation and method-selection time; no repeatable clerical pipeline is established for this task.

assumptions: The baseline is substantive impact research, excluding unattended computational runtime.
Observation validation and method checks remain in s1; no free attribution or pollution-effect flag is assumed.
Preparation already allocated to broader research tasks is not counted again here.
No new automation service or added upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Attribution methods and repeated preparation burden
research_questions: Which repeatable data preparation steps are separable from scientific attribution and not already scripted?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Impact research judgement remains; existing compute execution earns no credit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct wind assessment, integration and validation studies

steps.what: Define wind assessment methods and validate measurements, periods, heights and reference datasets
Calculate specified wind summaries, comparison statistics and validation diagnostics for the study
outputs: traceable wind study statistics and diagnostics

steps.what: Conduct wind assessment, integration or validation by interpreting diagnostics and site-specific limitations
inputs: traceable wind study statistics and diagnostics

tasks.design: Use native statistical operations in {DATA_PLATFORM} or controlled {SPREADSHEET} calculations before a new batch runner. Retain method choice, measurement validity and integration conclusions with the scientist in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated summaries and diagnostic calculations can be prepared manually between datasets.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit wind statistics and comparison operations can be rerun with recorded parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Judge representativeness, site effects and whether validation supports the intended use.
tasks.human_edge: Connect statistical diagnostics to physical wind conditions and study purpose.
tasks.altitude: Make routine calculations reproducible while retaining wind-study judgement.

reach.task: Clarify study requirements and physical site constraints

evidence.claim: Repeated wind statistics can be calculated from a checked specification; this task-specific design and saving are model knowledge.

assumptions: Measurement operators supply timestamps, wind speed and direction, units, measurement height, instrument ID, location and calibration metadata; their existing acquisition time receives no saving here.
In s1 the scientist captures and verifies those fields, period alignment, missingness rules, reference versions and exact calculation choices; all focal preparation remains in its 30 hours.
Two added other-role hours cover operator metadata corrections; eight added focal hours cover method and regression upkeep.
Missing metadata or failed diagnostics return to manual investigation in s1 and interpretation in s3; no automatic study-validity verdict is created.
Native calculation features come first, and already scripted summaries earn no new saving; broader research preparation excludes these same minutes.
research_questions: Does repeated calculation automation save time after measurement validation and method maintenance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross 25 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 17. E1 range 0-8 allows existing scripts and site-specific methods; study interpretation remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct numerical climate simulations to investigate weather patterns

steps.what: Specify numerical simulations of climate conditions, model assumptions and regional or global boundaries
Conduct simulation checks and interpret climate results to understand or predict weather patterns

tasks.design: Retain simulation configuration and scientific checks using {DATA_PLATFORM} and {DOCS}. The existing solver computes outputs after configuration and before review; its unattended runtime is outside the human labour denominator.
tasks.previous_blocker: A completed simulation can still contain invalid physical or numerical assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing computing infrastructure executes configured climate models.
tasks.still_hard: Establish that simulated patterns are physically and numerically credible.
tasks.human_edge: Choose valid assumptions and challenge model output.
tasks.altitude: Own simulation validity and limits of inference.

reach.task: Evaluate numerical stability and boundary assumptions

evidence.claim: Numerical simulation already relies on computational execution; shorter runtime alone establishes no saving in scientist configuration and interpretation.

assumptions: The baseline is scientist configuration, execution checks and interpretation rather than unattended solver runtime.
Existing computing infrastructure produces simulation outputs between s1 and s2; no newly free human input production is assumed.
Data preparation and general model-development minutes allocated elsewhere are excluded from this simulation baseline.
No new service or added upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Is repeated simulation setup measurable separately from scientific specification and existing batch execution?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Scientific setup and interpretation remain; existing solver runtime receives no labour credit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Estimate regional effects of global warming over time

steps.what: Select global warming scenarios, geographic regions, time horizons and supported impact indicators
Extract specified regional climate projections and assemble time-horizon comparison tables
Estimate effects of global warming for the region while assessing uncertainty and impact limitations

tasks.design: Use native regional subset and export tools in {DATA_PLATFORM} before building repeated extraction into {SPREADSHEET} comparisons. Retain scenario choice, impact assessment and uncertainty interpretation with the scientist in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable regional projection values may be repeatedly extracted across scenarios and horizons.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit region, variable and time selections can drive repeatable dataset extraction.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a projected climate change from a defensible regional impact claim.
tasks.human_edge: Choose relevant scenarios and explain what their projections cannot establish.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated projection extraction while retaining regional impact judgement.

reach.task: Assess regional exposure and impact pathways

evidence.claim: Explicit selections can automate repeated regional projection extraction; this exact design and its saving are model knowledge.

assumptions: Projection providers publish versioned scenarios, variables, units, grids, periods and uncertainty metadata; their existing modelling work receives no focal labour credit.

In s1 the scientist verifies and captures dataset versions, scenario IDs, geographic geometry, coordinate reference, baseline and future periods, indicators, units and aggregation choices; all focal capture and applicability checks remain in its 40 hours.
Missing metadata or unsupported indicators return to manual extraction and interpretation; no automatic regional-risk category is assumed.
Seven extra focal hours cover dataset schema, selection and regression upkeep; two other-role hours cover curator metadata clarification.
Native exports come first, and already automated extraction earns no new saving; general research preparation excludes these narrower extraction minutes.
unknowns: Dataset access and native export coverage
research_questions: Does repeatable regional extraction save time after scenario selection, metadata checks and upkeep?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80; gross 20 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 13. E1 range 0-6 allows existing export tools and changing projection schemas; impact judgement remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated wind calculations and projection extraction while retaining scientific attribution and simulation judgement.
role.ambitious_version: An atmospheric scientist who repeats checked calculations with less manual preparation and retains responsibility for physical validity and environmental conclusions.
